text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Bonn wants transport of nuclear waste to north German depot to go ahead despite protests.
- Structural crisis in German building sector will continue into next deacde, Ifo institute predicts.
- Labour Minister Norbert Bluem warns his critics against cutting pensions.
- Institute of German Industry (IW) says pension contributions will stabilise at around 22.5 percent.
- Vehicle tax reform plans remain controversial.
HANDELSBLATT
- Compromise close within ruling Christian Democrats over pension reform.
- Latest Konjunkturbarometer survey records further increase in business optimism in eastern Germany for February.
- Opposition Social Democrats want more active employment policy to be included in the "Masstricht II" treaty.
- Bonn wants to allow tolls to finance new road building.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Parliament condemns use of violence in protests against transport of nuclear waste.
- Conflict within Greens party in North Rhine-Westphalia over party's coalition with Social Democrats in state government.
- Rhine reaches high-water level.
- Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer says consolidation is order of the day for European nations' budgets.
DIE WELT
- Constitutional Court rejects complaint against European Union citizens' right to vote in German local elections.
- Social Democrats (SPD) want tougher penalties for child abuse.
- Wage talks for construction sector begin in Frankfurt.
- SPD wants to stimulate economy through small state-financed loans for business community.
